scenario_text: An NBFC wants to build an AI-based credit risk scoring engine but they're not sure exactly what data sources to use or what the model architecture should look like. There's significant technical risk — they've never built ML systems before. Budget is uncertain and depends on initial results. They want to build a proof of concept first before committing to full development.

requirements.statement: The system shall be capable of integrating with multiple external data sources for credit risk assessment
requirements.business_justification: Access to diverse data sources is crucial for accurate credit risk scoring; initial data sources may not be sufficient
requirements.assumptions: Data sources are available and can be integrated via APIs or data dumps
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can successfully ingest and process data from at least three external sources
applicable_regulations: Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks (including RRBs) and AIFIs §3.3 (RBI/2024-25 Fraud Risk Management) [revised 2024]

requirements.statement: The system shall be able to handle and process large datasets for training and testing the credit risk model
requirements.business_justification: Accurate credit risk scoring requires processing of extensive datasets; system must be scalable
requirements.assumptions: Data storage and processing infrastructure is available and sufficient
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can process and analyze datasets of at least 1 million records without significant performance degradation

requirements.statement: The system shall be capable of training and deploying multiple machine learning models for credit risk assessment
requirements.business_justification: Multiple models may be required to account for different credit risk scenarios; system must be able to adapt
requirements.assumptions: Data scientists have expertise in ML model development and deployment
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can successfully train and deploy at least two different ML models with comparable performance

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a proof of concept (POC) for the credit risk scoring engine before committing to full development
requirements.business_justification: POC will help mitigate technical risk and ensure feasibility of the project
requirements.assumptions: POC will be successful and provide valuable insights for full development
requirements.acceptance_criteria: POC demonstrates feasibility of the system and provides a clear roadmap for full development

requirements.statement: The system shall be developed with a flexible architecture to accommodate changing requirements and data sources
requirements.business_justification: Requirements and data sources may change over time; system must be adaptable
requirements.assumptions: Requirements and data sources will change over time
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can be easily modified to accommodate changes in requirements and data sources
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §19 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]

requirements.statement: The system shall track and display the status of each data source integration attempt, including successes and failures, for auditing and troubleshooting purposes.
requirements.business_justification: The scenario implies significant technical risk and uncertainty in data source selection, suggesting the need for visibility into integration attempts.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system logs all data source integration attempts, and the status of each attempt is displayed in a dashboard for the development team.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow administrators to configure and manage user roles and permissions for accessing and modifying the credit risk model and data sources.
requirements.business_justification: The scenario implies a need for flexibility and adaptability in the system architecture, suggesting the need for role-based access control.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system has a role-based access control system, and administrators can configure user roles and permissions through a web interface.
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §3(a) (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall be able to handle a minimum of 10,000 data points per hour, with an average response time of less than 2 seconds for model predictions.
requirements.business_justification: The scenario mentions handling large datasets, implying a need for scalability and performance.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system can handle a minimum of 10,000 data points per hour, and the average response time for model predictions is less than 2 seconds.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user-friendly interface for data source configuration and model training, with clear instructions and error messages.
requirements.business_justification: The scenario implies a need for usability and accessibility, particularly for non-technical stakeholders.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system has a user-friendly interface for data source configuration and model training, with clear instructions and error messages.

requirements.statement: The system shall store all data sources and model outputs in a secure and auditable manner, with version control and change tracking.
requirements.business_justification: The scenario implies a need for data management and governance, particularly given the sensitive nature of credit risk data.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system stores all data sources and model outputs in a secure and auditable manner, with version control and change tracking.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a dashboard for monitoring model performance and data source integration status, with real-time updates and alerts.
requirements.business_justification: The scenario implies a need for visibility and monitoring, particularly given the technical risk and uncertainty in data source selection.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system provides a dashboard for monitoring model performance and data source integration status, with real-time updates and alerts.

implied_rejected.statement: The system shall notify the development team and stakeholders of any failed model training or deployment attempts, including the reason for failure.

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Cyber Security Framework in Banks §15 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall detect and log cyber security incidents and support reporting them to RBI (and CERT-In) within the mandated timelines.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Requirements expected to change
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "An NBFC wants to build an AI-based credit risk scoring engine but they're not sure exactly what data sources to use or what the model architecture should look like."
risk_register.consequence: Work built early is discarded as the scope moves.
risk_register.mitigation: Deliver in short increments and keep the backlog prioritised with the product owner.
evidence: An NBFC wants to build an AI-based credit risk scoring engine but they're not sure exactly what data sources to use or what the model architecture should look like.

risk_register.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC/NPL time servers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: Industry practice (OWASP API Security Top 10)).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §8.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy.

risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "There's significant technical risk — they've never built ML systems before."
risk_register.consequence: Estimates are wrong and design mistakes are found late.
risk_register.mitigation: Spike the riskiest technical question first and bring in experienced review.
